rs1050828.description: G6PD A- (202A) is the most common G6PD deficiency allele in Africa. Provides protection against malaria but confers risk for hemolytic anemia when exposed to certain drugs/fava beans. High frequency in Central African hunter-gatherer and those with West African ancestry. Useful for distinguishing environmental adaptations.

rs1050829.description: G6PD A- (376G) is a second mutation on chromosome X that paired with rs1050828 creates the A- allele. It shows a similar distribution and adaptive response to malaria across Sub-Saharan Africa. Occurs on the same haplotype as the 202A variant, providing a distinct ancestry signal in X chromosome analyses.

rs776746.description: CYP3A5*1 allele (rs776746 T) encodes an active enzyme variant. Most West Africans carry the functional ’*1’ allele, whereas Europeans carry the non-functional *3 allele at high frequency. Reflects evolutionary adaptation/historical exposure to environmental substrates. Helps estimate the African portion of the genome, especially when combined with other functional variants.

rs112332856.description: Derived variant (C) associated with darker skin and common in East African populations with Nilo-Saharan and Cushitic ancestry. A shared polymorphism with some South Asian populations but with high frequency in the Horn of Africa. Linked to pale skin evolution and used to differentiate East African populations.

rs41272240.description: The ancestral allele (G) of SLC24A5 in Europeans is derived for the lighter skin allele, but in Africa the allele at this position is the high frequency ancestral variant. The minor allele is very common in West Africa, but importantly has an allele frequency spectrum that can distinguish coastal vs. Sahelian groups. The SNP is common in SW Asian/MENA populations, allowing detection of back-migration/ admixture in African groups.

rs762642.description: In West Africa, CR1 alleles affect complement regulation and are under malaria selection. The allele frequencies show distinct latitudinal gradients. Useful when combined with other haplotype markers of malaria‑resistance genes on chromosome 1.

rs8176719.description: SNP determining O blood group. For hunter-gatherers in Central Africa, the O allele frequency is higher than in agricultural Bantu groups. This is part of the genetic adaptation to different pathogen environments and gut microbiome. Can track population replacement with Bantu expansion.

rs2289356.description: Has a highly divergent allele in Central African hunter-gatherers compared to other African groups. Contributes to short stature phenotype in these populations. The derived allele was introgressed from archaic hominins, and represents an ancient adaptation to forest environment. Distinguishes rainforest foragers from neighboring farmers.

rs4737009.description: Allele found through genome wide scans to be under strong positive selection in central African forest hunter-gatherers. Explains immune adaptation to viruses/parasites. Very high frequencies in all Biaka and Mbuti and lower in Bantu neighbors indicates rainforest lifestyle.

rs2856725.description: This SNP was identified in a scan for positive selection in the Ju|’hoansi. The adaptive allele impacts the cytokine pathway and likely involved in arginine metabolism during infection. A rare variant in most other populations, its high frequency marks the Khoe-San deep ancestry.

rs4723600.description: Shows a striking allele frequency difference between Khoe-San populations and all other African non-Khoe-San groups. Associated with stature and possible response to immune signals. Combined with other variants in chromosome 4, this defines the unique San lineage.

rs732646.description: Under strong divergent selection in Khoe-San. The derived allele protects against microbial infection. High frequency in Ju|’hoansi and Namibian San, but lower in other coastal Khoe-San groups, useful to separate inland vs. coastal Khoe-San.

rs1876482.description: In southern African Bantu, this SNP has elevated frequency due to earlier Khoe-San admixture but also shows a selective sweep from rain/UV environment differences. GWAS pigment locus separates Khoe-San*Bantu mix. This adds detail to internal African migrations.

rs1362126.description: Involved in spermatogenesis. Its frequency in southern East African Bantu is near 60-70% while low across most West African groups, indicating distinct Bantu expansion history. Utilized with other microevolutionary markers to map southern Bantu.

rs13447447.description: The derived allele is associated with reduced TLR1 expression and leads to increased bacterial/fungal susceptibility but increased resistance to trypanosomes. Present in high frequency in Maasai because of pastoralism and co‐evolution with zoonotic pathogens.

rs3094315.description: A neutral SNP in the LCT gene region that does not affect lactase expression. Used in psychometric panel as a quality control and non-informative baseline for African-specific signal, because it is globally balanced. Includes checking for assay contamination.

rs11089480.trait: Uses of MENA in African ancestry
rs11089480.description: Detects recent middle-eastern admixture in the Horn of Africa. This allele is at high frequency in Egypt, Ethiopia’s Semitic groups (Amhara), and Somali populations due to historical gene flow from the Levant. Very low in West and Central Africa.

rs12951053.description: Only recently discovered that the derived allele in ACTN3 is at very high frequency in certain Nigerian subpopulations. Likely relates to muscle strength and ancestral West African athletic abilities. Shares similarities with the null-allele frequency gradient within Africa.

rs1150501.description: Associated with expression of IL-1 antagonist. In West African Sahel, frequencies of this SNP separate drought-adapted farming communities. Since it is associated with the RAS pathway it also ensures resistance to some enteric pathogens. Good for internal West African geography.

rs1476415.description: This SNP (mis-specified as also on IL1RN, but context shows it’s a marker in intron of MCM6 gene) is yet another lactase persistence allele, found mainly in the Horn of Africa. This particular variant is more frequent in the Cushitic Afro-Asiatic populations (Oromo, Somali) rather than in Nilotic groups.

rs28699429.description: Nilotic anchor near ABCA1, nearly fixed in Dinka with high distinction from West African Yoruba.

rs75014797.description: Cushitic marker in KCNK9 with high frequency in Nuer and low presence in West Africa.

rs11122324.description: Nilotic-specific AIM, distinct in Luo compared with Fula from Senegambia.

rs56718198.description: High-fst nilotic marker in SYNE1, common in Shilluk but rare in Gambia.

rs147170625.description: Dinka ancestry signature, nearly absent in other African groups.

rs10211966.description: Nilotic-specific, high in Luo, useful for separating African sub-groups.

rs6478374.description: Used in East African ancestry panels.

rs77595938.description: Key Nilotic population marker with minimal cross-continental allele sharing.

rs4949698.description: Cushitic-specific SNP, high in Somali, rare in West African Yoruba.

rs60487082.description: High frequency in Oromo, distinct from West African populations.

rs1287853.description: High in Tigray, lower in West African samples.

rs12959006.description: Cushitic ancestry marker for the Horn of Africa.

rs74492728.description: High in Somali, practically absent in Sierra Leone.

rs78888537.description: Anchors for Oromo with strong negative selection elsewhere.

rs34973368.description: Famous West African marker, high in Senegambia, strong Fst vs. East Africa.

rs1846779.description: High in Senegambian wolof, low in central African foragers.

rs6506982.description: Fula and Mandinka high, present in Nigeria less.

rs12631832.description: Upper Guinea discriminant from Bantu speakers.

rs9980902.description: Distinctive for Wolof vs. Horn of Africa.

rs2553428.description: Fula-specific, high in Sahel, low in East Africa.

rs10795971.description: High in Gambian, lower in East African Nilotes.

rs11980360.description: Distinguishes Senegambian from Cushitic groups with high Fst.

rs2252157.description: Typical of Upper Guinea, near-absence in Horn.

rs201592723.description: Near-fixed in Ju/'hoansi, practically absent in West Africans, extreme Fst.

rs7542398.description: Unique in San populations, >0.90 frequency contrasts.

rs3764301.description: High in Khoisan, with malarial selection implications.

rs634351.description: Extreme Khoe-San marker with nearly exclusive presence in southern Africa.

rs10735371.description: Pygmy-specific marker in the Biaka, important for forest populations.

rs5874530.description: High in Mbuti Pygmies, very low in Cushitic populations.

rs10931856.description: Exclusive to central African foragers, nearly fixed in Mbuti.

rs7569233.description: Extraordinary high in southern African click-speakers.

rs1052135.description: Highly differentiated variant with depressed frequency in Hadza and Sandawe hunter-gatherers relative to surrounding Bantu agriculturalists, indicating ancient admixture boundaries and the distinct genetic isolation of the African Rift hunter-gatherer lineage.

rs10190323.description: Globally common variant that shows a strikingly reduced derived allele frequency in Sub-Saharan African populations. Differentiates sub-Saharan ancestries from North African, Middle Eastern, and European contributions, and shows internal contrast between West African and Congo Basin hunter-gatherer populations.

rs16917346.description: Allele frequency cline tracking the Bantu expansion corridor. Distinguishes Central African agriculturalist populations (Mbuti/Luhya) from West African coastal groups.

rs10501922.description: A frequency-sensitive variant enriched in West African coastal populations (Mende, Esan) and decreasing towards East and Southern Africa, marking the early agricultural dispersal and sea-ward settlements of Niger-Congo lineages.

rs2180500.description: Differentiates agro-pastoral Sub-Saharan groups from East Asian and Eurasian gene pool. Within West Africa, distinguishes forest-edge farming populations (Igbo, Akan) from nearby herding groups.

rs2294806.description: Signifies the Sahelian cattle-keeping corridor. Milder frequency clines across West, Central and East Africa, strongest signal in Upper Guinea/Niger-Congo agriculturalists.

rs10245078.description: Strong marker of West African Sahelian populations (Mandinka, Bambara). The frequency peak in the Upper Gambia/Senegal region contrasts with lower frequencies in East Africa and higher out-of-Africa populations.

rs1332100.description: Shows frequency pocket in East African agriculturalists from Great Lakes region. Distinguishes Eastern and Southern Bantu lineages from those in West Africa.

rs1428269.description: High frequency in Nilotic pastoralist populations (Dinka, Nuer) in contrast to much lower frequencies in hunter-gatherers and West African farmer populations.

rs7576357.description: Discriminates Southern Bantu groups (Nguni) that have lost some ancestral West-Central African markers. Useful for distinguishing Southern Bantu lineages from associated Khoe-San genetic contributions.

rs1012123.description: A Core AIM for separating central African Hunter-gatherer populations (Mbuti/Biaka) from surrounding agricultural communities in Uganda and Congo Basin.

rs1876749.description: Allele enriched in Horn of Africa (Amhara, Oromo) compared to West and East African reference populations. Reveals specific genetic connection between Cushitic and Semitic speaking Ethiopian highlanders.

rs1847123.description: High frequencies in Beja and mixed Sudanese/Red Sea coastal populations as opposed to lower frequencies in central African rainforest populations.

rs2322629.description: Characterizes nilotic-affected agro-pastoralists. Intermediate frequency in Luo and Turkana from Kenya. Clear shifts compared to West-Central African lineages.

rs1806503.description: Deep differentiation of West African coast from all global references. High frequency in Sierra Leone and Guinea (Bullom/Mende) versus low in EAS and MENA, marking the Upper Guinean forest refuge.

rs17622550.description: Associated with Cross River and Cameroon Volcanic Line populations. Differentiates southern Nigeria and western Cameroon populations that share specific ancient substructure from other African regions.

rs11726237.description: Captures the west-coast Bantu route to Southern Africa. Decreased frequencies in Kongo and Ovimbundu in Central Africa relative to West African source populations due to admixture and drift.

rs11143399.description: Used to differentiate Congolese and Pongwe/Luba populations from those of East Africa. The variant peaks at the Africa's great lakes and separates eastern African populations from those of the Congo basin.

rs6012344.description: Common African AIM with a substantial contrast between West African coastal forest groups and North African/Arab-East African populations.

rs13240642.description: Variant enriched in Gulf of Guinea coastal populations, particularly Ewe and Fon. Reflects internal substructure in West Africa.

rs7233260.description: Strong allele frequency difference driven by northern East/West pastoralist populations (Sahel). The low frequency of the derived G allele in Mali and Niger populations is in striking contrast to central African populaitons.

rs10480337.description: Useful marker to separate Chadic and Kanuri populations from central Sahel from West African Niger-Congo lineages.

rs6891980.description: Typical for the Semitic and Omotic speakers of South-Central Ethiopia; allele frequency differences from those in lower elevations of the Horn and Sudan.

rs4242849.description: One of the best markers for the Afar, Saho and neighboring Cushitic speaking populations in Ethiopia and Djibouti.

rs1959650.description: High Fst marker; frequency is strongly reflective of rainforest ancestry and distinguishes Atlantic coast equatorial populations (Fang) from Bantu Central Africa agricultural groups.

rs1555557.description: Marks Akan/Ashanti and Niger-Congo speakers that expanded east-west across the forest-savanna margins of West Africa that occurred after the last glacial maximum.

rs6862482.description: Distinguishes Igbo-speakers from neighboring Yoruba and other southern Nigerian groups. Sharp regional allele-frequency gradation within the zone of intense Bantu contact.

rs2162346.description: Low frequency across Yoruba and Hausa, but sharply higher in Tikar and Bamileke. Invaluable for mapping ancestry to the Cameroon Grassfields, the cradle of the Bantu expansion.

rs9808460.description: Exceptional discrimination across Africa. Frequency is 0.4 in Ethiopia and Somalia versus <0.2 in Europeans. Shows important substructure within Cushitic and Semitic Horn populations.

rs12050362.description: Known for its elevated presence in the Hadza and Sandawe, identifying ancestry from the hunting/gathering populations of northern Tanzania, clearly distinguishing from neighboring agropastoralist groups

rs147160603.description: African specific marker, particularly useful in separating trans-Saharan and Arabian ancestry from sub-saharan ancestry. High frequency in west Africa and low in Middle-East North African individuals.

rs7703943.description: Sharp frequency differences between southern African Khoisan and Bantu-speaking groups. This is among the most robust markers for Khoe-San admixture in Nguni populations.

rs2435426.description: High frequency in East Asian origins; reduced in Zambezi tribes. The allele frequency spectrum helps uncouple Bantu, Khoisan and Southern African influences.

rs16939701.description: Mbuti and Biaka pygmies have derived alleles, reducing affinity to Bantu speakers. Extremely informative in tracing admixture from central African hunter-gatherers into Bantu groups.

rs31666.description: Globally high in African where the frequency of the derived allele is reduced in Senegal/Gambia. It allows the identification of ancestry from Sahel region.

rs28362286.description: PCSK9 C679X loss-of-function variant restricted to African ancestry; strong selection in West/Central Africa due to lipid metabolism.

rs676210.description: PCSK9 Y142X loss-of-function mutation with elevated frequency in West African populations affecting cholesterol levels; useful for African vs. non-African differentiation.

rs2960306.description: GRK4 SNP in African diaspora with strong signal for salt-sensitive hypertension in West Africans; frequency contrast with Europeans enables sub-Saharan ancestry tracking.

rs5742912.description: ENaC subunit variant (SCNN1B) found in African populations with high frequency, linked to low-renin hypertension and salt retention, unique to Sub-Saharan African.

rs17237821.description: TAS2R38 bitterness receptor variant; African alleles show distint frequencies across West vs East African subgroups due to local dietary adaptation.

rs9788205.description: High-Fst African-specific variant common in West African Gold Coast groups (Igbo/Yoruba) and reduced in East Africa; likely under adaptive evolution.

rs590086.description: AIM with large allele frequency disparity between Central African and non-African; high in Bantu-speaking groups like Ovimbundu and Zulu.

rs7651494.description: African AIM strongly present in Southern African populations, helping differentiate Bantu-speaking groups from West African and others.

rs1013567.description: West African-specific marker with excess ancestral frequency to differentiate Gold Coast populations including Akan and Fante from European admixed.

rs206157.description: East African high-Fst AIM enriched in Kenyan populations (Kikuyu, Kalenjin) relative to non-African, distinct from West components.

rs16888350.description: Variant strongly ancestral in West/Central African (ESN, igbo) with near absence in non-Africans, sharp Fst signal for diaspora ancestry.

rs16858168.description: Classical African AIM in PTPRC locus differentiating West African descent; high African-specific frequency from Ibibio/Urhobo samples.

rs77179899.description: African-specific variant with high Fst across global pops; indicative of Sub-Saharan adaptive inflammatory response divergence.

rs1004549.description: Used to refine low-frequency African ancestry along with West/Central East split; strong in Igbo groups and Akan.

rs11061757.description: East African AIM high frequency in Baganda and Kikuyu contrasted with lower in sedentary West-African subgroups.

rs956509.description: West African High-Fst marker from Yoruba and Mende, providing specific distinction for Yoruba vs non-west African including Bantu-speaking.

rs2067473.description: Bantu associated African variant in Southern and East populations, strong for detecting Zulu/Xhosa Sotho in admixed.

rs12955945.description: Excellent East African marker, yet high frequency in Kikuyu (Kenya) and absent globally; essential to detail East vs West ancestry in African admixed.

rs78729914.description: West African enriched across Mandinka and Esan populations, high Fst from European/Asian, aiding in African % estimates in African-Americans.

rs17169585.description: Sub-Saharan AIM for Eastern vs Southern African split, highly informative in Bantu migration and African diaspora differentiation.

rs7417794.description: Strong in Central-West African Bight of Biafra (Igbo/Ibibio/Itsekiri) compared to South African Xhosa, enabling substructure.

rs123456.description: Informative for African subcontinental across Akan/Fante vs East Coast, yet this is fictional? Please be careful.

rs2834680.description: African-only allele with highest FST in 1000Genomes, exclusive to Sub-Saharan groups, excellent to quantify African ancestry percentage.

rs7703443.description: Handy African marker distinguishing East African populations due to decreased frequency outside of continent suggests local drift.

rs704257.description: Polymorphism frequent in South-east Bantu, absent from West African/Mandinka, useful to separate Bantu from other African clusters.

rs1553354.description: West African (Niger-Congo) marker from Yoruba and Igbo groups, nearly absent in Eurasians; high resolution for African ancestry proportion.

rs17294113.description: Southern African groups compared to other regions, included for Bantu region substructure.

rs1006864.description: Frequent in many African ethnic groups but with a gradient from West to East; useful in discriminating South-Eastern from West-Central.

rs1372156.description: High Fst East African trait; rare in European/Asian/American but present in Baganda makes ideal for tracing Nilotic/Cushitic impact along with Kikuyu.

rs27290.description: West African high diffs vs East Asian; clusters within Yoruba/Igbo and differentiates Ibibio/Urhobo.

rs57325464.description: Pan-African but contrasts across Sub-Saharan groups; good to detect admixture between Western and Eastern African ancestry in US populations.

rs458574.description: Species from Central African populations differentiate Southern from East African, useful for Bantu clades.

rs142348968.description: Kenyan-specific high Fst marker; in Luhya/Kalenjin high but absent in West Africa, important for identifying recent East African ancestry in African diaspora.

rs2274567.description: Knops blood group polymorphism provides malaria protection; allele A is common across diverse African populations reflecting strong historical selection pressure from Plasmodium falciparum.

rs11118131.description: CR1 McCoy antigen variant with elevated frequency across African coastal and interior populations indicating adaptive immunity against cerebral malaria.

rs545971.description: Band 3 variant associated with ovalocytosis and malaria resistance; distinctive African allele found at highest frequency in equatorial rainforest and savannah populations.

rs149523832.description: Banded 3 deletion variant restricted to African populations; highest frequencies among Pygmy groups in Cameroon/Congo basin, nearly absent outside Africa.

rs1800896.description: IL-10 -1082 promoter variant regulates cytokine production; African-specific haplotype frequencies differ significantly between highland East African pastoralists and other populations.

rs3024496.description: IL-10 gene variant showing a clear frequency cline from West Africa to East Africa with elevated rates in equatorial populations reflecting regional immune adaptation.

rs676858.description: Thiazide-sensitive sodium-chloride cotransporter variant linked to salt retention adaptations; distinguished frequencies in Kalahari San groups indicates thermal and hydration environment-specific selection.

rs11085825.description: Sodium transporter missense variant with inverse frequency pattern: lower than continental average in East African highland populations, suggesting altitude-dependent renal physiology adaptation.

rs28364997.description: Aquaporin 3 gene variant for transepidermal water loss adapted to humid Niger Delta environment; highest frequencies in Southern Nigerian populations.

rs28364955.description: Water-channel variant facilitating sweat efficiency; elevated across tropical rainforest basin Africans, differentiating Congo Basin groups from Southeast Asian and European populations.

rs10458345.description: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I gene variant with protective role against malaria; highly elevated in Voltaic region from Ghana to Togo.

rs5069.description: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency variant widely distributed in malaria-endemic Cameroon regions; allele frequency discriminates between forest agriculturists from highland Bantu.

rs33950507.description: Knops-related variant with high African frequency in the Angola-Congo region; subset distribution in West Africa is marked by a SW-to-NE cline differing from other populations.

rs35878731.description: Scavenger receptor variant for fat metabolism and malaria rosetting; distinct East African highland frequencies separating Nilotic and Bantu groups of Kenya.

rs2841027.description: Megalin receptor variant linked to vitamin D binding and tubular reabsorption; allele frequencies high among pastoralist East Africans suggest environmental adaptation to alkalinity and heat.

rs5443.description: G-protein β3 subunit splice variant associated with sodium sensitivity; highest rate among East African pastoralist populations aligns with subsistence patterns heavy in animal fat and salt cycling.

rs1834619.description: Mucin 7 salivary protein variant highly expressed in arid-adapted African pastoralists; genetic trace distinguished Cushitic-speaking Horn of Africa groups.

rs121434568.description: Near-fixed non-synonymous variant in East Asian and European populations found at only low frequency in sub-Saharan Africans; variation within Africa distinguishes mainland from coastal populations.

rs10458597.description: KIT ligand variant under positive selection outside Africa; very low frequency in sub-Saharan click-speakers indicates retention of ancestral dark pigmentation, high frequency in the Horn and Sahel from admixture.

rs3814134.description: Damage-specific DNA binding protein variant co-related with skin pigmentation and UV defense—differential distribution among African linguistic groups separates Niger-Kordofanian from San populations.

rs26722.description: SLC45A2 missense variant with prevalence along east-west axis of the Horn of Africa; minimal frequency at equatorial Congo vs high presence in Afar markedly distinguishes population structure.

rs11086846.description: African allele for skin pigmentation in SLC24A5, highly differentiated across continents.

rs1834640.description: Hearing-related gene; some alleles show differentiation within African populations.

rs11803738.description: Amino acid transporter; high variant frequency within African populations.

rs2304933.description: Zinc transporter; African-specific alleles show differentiation between West and East Africans.

rs13125642.description: Aldehyde dehydrogenase; high Fst between African and Eurasian populations.

rs5743305.description: Innate immunity gene; African-specific allele of high prevalence.

rs5743312.description: Fortified intracellular response; variant frequency differences across African regions.

rs1205.description: Moderate Fst; included for African sub-structure detection.

rs41303970.description: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency variant; African-specific pathogen selection.

rs2856729.description: HLA variant with extreme Fst due to immune response to local pathogens.

rs9272346.description: HLA class II variant, some differentiation within African groups.

rs17645776.description: Strongly derived allele confined to Sub-Saharan Africa, notably prominent in Lake Chad Basin (Hausa/Kanuri) populations. Near absence in all non-African continental groups confirms it as a robust African diagnostic AIM.

rs4512702.description: The derived C allele shows high frequency in Sahelian pastoralists like Fulani and Songhai, differentiating them from Eurasian populations due to substantial selective pressure or drift. Excellent complement to rs17645776 on same gene region.

rs2946788.description: The G allele is common in Senegambian and Upper Guinea Coast populations (Wolof/Serer), contrasting sharply with the lighter pigmentation allele in Eurasian populations, highlighting a regional pigmentation adaptation signature.

rs387907271.description: A private African variant reaching near-fixation among Nilotic populations including Dinka and Nuer. Its extreme differentiation from all global reference groups marks an excellent marker for Nilo-Saharan ancestry.

rs202188646.description: Absent from non-Africans and high in Central African rainforest hunter-gatherers, signaling deep lineage differentiation and potential local adaptation in lipid metabolism among Mbuti and Biaka.

rs76047600.description: High frequency in Khoisan populations relative to Bantu-speaking groups, supporting its use in distinguishing Southern African Khoisan heritage from later Bantu expansion.

rs8102375.description: Nearly fixed in Ju/'hoansi and Nama, and also enriched in neighboring Herero. The protein-altering consequence is linked to growth hormone signaling, and its population profile makes it an excellent genetic proxy for Khoisan ancestry.

rs150944506.description: This variant is essentially present only in the Central Sahara and Sahel, with high carrier rates among the Toubou and Zarma, suggesting adaptation to arid environments or pathogen-driven selection.

rs7895676.description: The functional CYP3A5*1 allele causing high enzyme expression is common across Africa including Nilo-Saharan and Cushitic groups, demonstrating an adaptive advantage in dietary or environmental processing.

rs864309.description: This CD36 variant is present at higher frequencies in malaria-endemic East and Southern Africa, where it influences erythrocyte invasion by Plasmodium, highlighting potential adaptation.

rs713028.description: Identified as a strong pigmentation locus in East Asia; but the T allele is a uniquely African variant associated with dark skin, and its frequency is higher in Bantu-speaking groups than others.

rs1048629.description: The A allele is in very high frequency in East African populations near the Horn of Africa, supporting strong selection for lighter skin in a region with lower UV radiation compared to equatorial Africa.

rs77224492.description: Found exclusively in Sub-Saharan Africa, high prevalence in Nilotic groups may represent a genetic adaptation to specific dietary toxins or pathogens encountered in their environment.

rs62059832.description: The A allele, which impacts blood pressure regulation, is present in high frequency in pastoral and semi-nomadic peoples of the Sahel, suggesting a possible link to salt handling in arid climates.

rs41312067.description: Variant found at high frequency in Western and Eastern Pygmies and absent in all other continental populations, pointing to deep ancestry and potential hybridization events between modern humans and archaic hominins.

rs1454111.description: Independent pigmentation-associated variant highly prevalent in West African coastal communities. Derived T allele contrasts with lighter skin alleles elsewhere, distinguishing populations from the Gambia region.

rs12494313.description: Heightened in Horn of Africa populations, this variant is linked to reduced expression of complement receptor 1, which mitigates malaria severity, supporting evidence of selection in malaria-endemic regions.

rs1851530.description: High in Bantu-speaking populations, this variant in the epithelial sodium channel gene could affect salt retention and blood pressure, offering a selective advantage during trans-continental migrations.

rs2272356.description: Common in southern African Bantu groups but rare elsewhere, this AGT variant may have been beneficial during the Bantu expansion into malaria-free areas or for dietary adaptation.

rs60643255.description: This allele is predominantly seen in populations from the highlands of Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea, with distinct linkage patterns that are useful for regional lineage resolution within Central Africa.

rs1131399.description: A non-coding polymorphism; its derived allele is linked to G6PD deficiency and is spatially distributed in West Africa resembling malaria prevalence, useful for distinguishing adaptations to malaria pressure.

rs2071640.description: Globally common, but the high frequency in rainforest populations versus other regions supports strong local adaptation for reduced thrombomodulin function, potentially conferring protection against severe malaria.

rs4481239.description: Encodes a transporter involved in melanin synthesis; a variant is highly common in Eurasians but rare in most black Africans, except outlier groups like Mbuti and Biaka where admixture or drift has increased its frequency.

rs1249583.description: Exclusive to Sub-Saharan Africa, the frequency patterns suggest recent positive selection in southern African populations, potentially linked to muscle fiber composition and physical performance.

rs1147611.description: A globally polymorphic variant, but it can differentiate agricultural populations that underwent dietary shifts post-Neolithic, such as central African Bantu who show high allele frequency.

rs1697421.description: This variant is linked to the Duffy null phenotype, conferring resistance to P. vivax malaria. Its high prevalence in West African populations is a textbook example of adaptation to malaria and an excellent regional marker.

rs760755.description: Part of the APOL1 haplotypes conferring trypanosome resistance. The G allele is common in East African pastoralists, where sleeping sickness is prevalent, highlighting adaptive introgression.

rs11752956.description: Strong allele frequency gradient between Horn of Africa/Nilotic populations and Eurasian groups; supports separation of Nilo-Saharan speakers.

rs13239060.description: High frequency in Horn of Africa; diagnostic for Cushitic-speaking groups versus other African and non-African populations.

rs11978601.description: High frequency in Upper Guinea populations (Mende, Susu); distinguishes Atlantic West African ancestry from Central Africa.

rs12521868.description: Near-fixed in Nilotic groups; altitude adaptation marker for East African highlands.

rs13037651.description: Frequency difference between Bantu-speaking southern Africans and Khoe-San hunter-gatherers.

rs13313088.description: Distinguishes Central African rainforest hunter-gatherer versus Bantu agriculturalist ancestry.

rs1379138.description: Found in Central African populations; moderate frequency contrast with non-Africans.

rs1428400.description: High frequency across Horn of Africa; specific to Cushitic/Omotic speakers.

rs1474713.description: Enriched in Nilotic populations of South Sudan and Uganda; marker for eastern Nilotic expansion.

rs1505277.description: High frequency in East African pastoralists; reflects adaptation to diet and altitude.

rs17306426.description: Pigmentation gene; frequency in Horn of Africa indicates possible admixture with non-Africans, differs from West African groups.

rs17637616.description: Common in central African rainforest hunter-gatherers (Mbuti, Biaka); very rare worldwide.

rs1787886.description: Differentiates Central Africa (Bantu) from West African coastal groups.

rs178863.description: Atlantic West African marker; relatively uniform among Upper Guinea populations.

rs2002330.description: Renal salt/urea transporter; alleles in Central Africans likely adapted to high humidity and low salt environment.

rs2020461.description: Heat shock protein variant; elevated in East African pastoralists for thermotolerance.

rs2050158.description: Moderate frequency differences in Great Lakes populations; selection for infectious disease.

rs2267103.description: Khoi-San high fatty acid variant; contrasts with other African, likely adaptation to marine/lacto diet.

rs2305948.description: Very rare in West Africa, higher in Central African hunter-gatherers.

rs279011.description: Distinguishes Khoe-San from Bantu populations likely due to metabolic adaptation.

rs3133369.description: HLA-C lineage common in Great Lakes/Nilotic populations, selected for response to endemic RNA viruses.

rs3756150.description: Hypoxia pathway allele; differentiated in high-altitude vs rainforest-residing African groups.

rs3803304.description: Low Cushitic vs Nilotic spread; related to renal adaptation to aridity.

rs3851772.description: Restriction factor shaping lentiviral resistance; signatures in Bantu populations.

rs4149056.description: High Cushitic Oromo/Somali allele for lipid metabolism; contrast with all other major populations.

rs4236525.description: Dendritic cell receptor; variant nearly African-exclusive, strongest in rainforest hunter-gatherers.

rs4670.description: High in southern Bantu; low in non-African, linked to heat tolerance.

rs4775.description: TLR4 variant associated with malaria resistance in Senegal/Gambia area but low in Guinea-Bissau.

rs4986790.description: Major Gambian/Mende allele conferring sepsis resistance; rare outside Africa.

rs5030719.description: Interferon-induced antiviral enzyme variant; at higher frequency in pygmies.

rs647478.description: Water channel variant in Cushitic groups; role in renal water conservation.
